title: Area of Parallelograms and Trapezia
summary: See where the formulae A = bh and A = ½(a + b)h come from, then use them to find areas, missing heights and missing sides in Checkpoint-style problems.

blocks.title: In the curriculum
items: Use what you know about **rectangles, squares and triangles** to work out (derive) the formulae for the area of a **parallelogram** and a **trapezium**. (8Gg.04)
Use the formulae to **calculate** the area of parallelograms and trapezia, and to find a missing length when the area is known. (8Gg.04)

blocks.text: 1. Key words

items: area
المساحة — the amount of flat space inside a shape, in square units (cm², m², mm²)
parallelogram
متوازي أضلاع — two pairs of parallel sides
trapezium (plural: trapezia)
شبه منحرف — at least one pair of parallel sides
base (b)
القاعدة — the side you measure the height from
perpendicular height (h)
الارتفاع العمودي — the distance between the parallel sides, measured at 90°
slant height / sloping side
الضلع المائل — a side that leans; it is NOT the height
derive
يستنتج — show where a formula comes from
formula (plural: formulae)
قانون — a rule written with letters

blocks.text: You already know: **area of a rectangle = length × width (b × h)**, **area of a square = side × side**, and **area of a triangle = ½ × base × perpendicular height**. Every formula on this page is built from these.
2. Area of a parallelogram

**Deriving the formula.** Cut a right-angled triangle off one end of the parallelogram (along the dashed height line) and slide it to the other end. The pieces make a **rectangle**. Nothing was added or removed, so the area has not changed.

blocks.caption: A parallelogram can be cut and rearranged into a rectangle with the same base b and the same height h.

blocks.text: The rectangle has length b and width h, so its area is b × h. Therefore:

blocks.title: Area of a parallelogram
blocks.text: **Area = base × perpendicular height**  →  **A = bh**. The height must be measured at **right angles** to the base, not along the sloping side.

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 370 182" width="370" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14"><polygon points="30,150 246,150 325.6,30 109.6,30" fill="#eaf1fb" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><line x1="109.6" y1="30" x2="109.6" y2="150" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><polyline points="119.6,150 119.6,140 109.6,140" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="117.6" y="95" font-weight="bold">5 cm</text><text x="138" y="172" text-anchor="middle">9 cm</text><text x="307.5" y="109.4" text-anchor="middle">6 cm</text></svg>
blocks.caption: The height is 5 cm (dashed, at 90° to the base). The sloping side, 6 cm, is not used for the area.

blocks.text: **Any side can be the base**, as long as you use the height that is perpendicular to *that* side. A useful result: parallelograms (and rectangles) with the **same base and the same height** always have the **same area**, however much they lean.
3. Area of a trapezium
A trapezium has two **parallel sides** (call them a and b) and a perpendicular height h between them. There are two good ways to derive the formula.

**Method 1 — two copies make a parallelogram.** Take two identical trapezia. Turn one upside down (rotate it 180°) and put it next to the other. Together they make a parallelogram with base **(a + b)** and height **h**.

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 540 194" width="540" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14"><polygon points="20,130 188,130 140,34 44,34" fill="#eaf1fb" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><text x="104" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">a</text><text x="92" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">b</text><line x1="74" y1="34" x2="74" y2="130" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><polyline points="84,130 84,120 74,120" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="82" y="87" font-weight="bold">h</text><text x="105" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">trapezium</text><line x1="205" y1="85" x2="234.6" y2="85" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2.2"/><polygon points="240,85 231,89 231,81" fill="#0f1b33" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="250,130 514,130 538,34 274,34" fill="#eaf1fb" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="418,130 514,130 538,34 370,34" fill="#e3f4e5" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="250,130 514,130 538,34 274,34" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><text x="334" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">a</text><text x="466" y="152" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">b</text><text x="322" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">b</text><text x="454" y="26" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">a</text><text x="394" y="182" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">parallelogram: base (a + b), height h</text></svg>
blocks.caption: Two identical trapezia fit together to make a parallelogram with base a + b.

blocks.text: Area of the parallelogram = (a + b) × h. One trapezium is **half** of it: area = ½(a + b)h.
**Method 2 — split into two triangles.** Draw a diagonal. The trapezium becomes two triangles with the same height h: one has base a, the other has base b.

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 540 185" width="540" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14"><polygon points="40,150 280,150 205,30" fill="#eaf1fb" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polygon points="40,150 205,30 85,30" fill="#fff4d6" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><line x1="40" y1="150" x2="205" y2="30" stroke="#c0392b" stroke-width="2"/><text x="160" y="172" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">a</text><text x="145" y="22" text-anchor="middle" font-weight="bold">b</text><line x1="205" y1="30" x2="205" y2="150" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><polyline points="215,150 215,140 205,140" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="213" y="95" font-weight="bold">h</text><text x="320" y="60">yellow triangle: ½ × b × h</text><text x="320" y="85">blue triangle: ½ × a × h</text><text x="320" y="120">total = ½ah + ½bh</text><text x="320" y="145" font-weight="bold">= ½(a + b)h</text></svg>
blocks.caption: A diagonal splits the trapezium into two triangles with the same height.

blocks.title: Area of a trapezium
blocks.text: **Area = ½ × (sum of the parallel sides) × perpendicular height**  →  **A = ½(a + b)h**. In words: add the parallel sides, multiply by the height, then halve. (You can halve first if that is easier: ½ of 4 = 2, then 2 × 16 = 32.)

blocks.title: القوانين بالعربي
items: متوازي الأضلاع = القاعدة × الارتفاع العمودي (A = bh). لو قصّيت مثلث من ناحية وحطيته في الناحية التانية هيبقى مستطيل.
شبه المنحرف = نص × (مجموع الضلعين المتوازيين) × الارتفاع: A = ½(a + b)h. نسختين منه بيعملوا متوازي أضلاع قاعدته a + b.
الارتفاع لازم يكون عمودي (زاوية 90°) — الضلع المايل مانستخدموش في المساحة.

blocks.text: 4. Method, step by step

items: **Name the shape** and write the formula: A = bh or A = ½(a + b)h.

**Find the right lengths**: for a parallelogram, the base and the perpendicular height; for a trapezium, the two parallel sides (look for arrows) and the height between them. Cross out any sloping length you do not need.
**Check the units** are the same (all cm or all m). Convert first if they are not.
**Substitute and calculate.** Show this line: it earns the method mark.
**Write square units**: cm², m², mm².

**Reverse questions** (area given, length missing): substitute what you know, then use inverse operations. For a trapezium, multiply the area by 2 first, then divide by the height (or by the sum of the parallel sides).

blocks.text: 5. Worked examples

**Worked example 1** [2 marks]
Work out the area of the parallelogram in section 2 (base 9 cm, sloping side 6 cm, perpendicular height 5 cm).

items: A = b × h. The height is the perpendicular one: 5 cm.
**Answer: 45 cm²**

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** 9 × 6 = 54 cm². The 6 cm side slopes, so it is not the height.

**Worked example 2** [2 marks]
Calculate the area of this trapezium.

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 310 172" width="310" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14"><polygon points="30,140 270,140 210,44 66,44" fill="#eaf1fb" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polyline points="219,144.9 226,140 219,135.1" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.6"/><polyline points="178.2,48.9 185.2,44 178.2,39.1" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.6"/><line x1="116" y1="44" x2="116" y2="140" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.8" stroke-dasharray="6 4"/><polyline points="126,140 126,130 116,130" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="124" y="97" font-weight="bold">4 cm</text><text x="150" y="162" text-anchor="middle">10 cm</text><text x="138" y="34" text-anchor="middle">6 cm</text></svg>
blocks.caption: Parallel sides 6 cm and 10 cm; perpendicular height 4 cm.

items: **Answer: 32 cm²**

blocks.text: **Common mistake:** ½ × 6 + 10 × 4 = 43. Add the parallel sides **first** (brackets!), then multiply.

**Worked example 3** [2 marks]
A parallelogram has area 56 cm² and base 8 cm. Work out its perpendicular height.

items: A = bh, so 56 = 8 × h.
**Answer: 7 cm**

blocks.text:
**Worked example 4** [2 marks]
A trapezium has parallel sides 7 m and 13 m. Its area is 60 m². Find the perpendicular height.

items: **Answer: 6 m**

blocks.text:
**Worked example 5** [3 marks]
A trapezium has area 45 cm² and height 6 cm. One of its parallel sides is 5 cm. Find the length of the other parallel side.

**Worked example 6** [4 marks]
A farmer's field is a trapezium. A bag of grass seed covers 50 m² and costs 85 Egyptian pounds. How much will it cost to cover the whole field?

blocks.svg: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 400 182" width="400" font-family="Arial, sans-serif" font-size="14"><polygon points="50,150 338,150 230,37.5 50,37.5" fill="#e3f4e5" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="2" stroke-linejoin="round"/><polyline points="62,150 62,138 50,138" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.5"/><polyline points="62,37.5 62,49.5 50,49.5" fill="none" stroke="#0f1b33" stroke-width="1.5"/><text x="194" y="172" text-anchor="middle">64 m</text><text x="140" y="27.5" text-anchor="middle">40 m</text><text x="42" y="98.8" text-anchor="end">25 m</text><text x="220" y="20" text-anchor="middle" font-size="13">NOT TO SCALE</text></svg>
blocks.caption: The field: parallel sides 40 m and 64 m, perpendicular height 25 m (a right-angled trapezium).

items: Number of bags = 1300 ÷ 50 = 26 bags (exactly, so no rounding needed).
**Answer: 2210 Egyptian pounds.**

blocks.text: In a right-angled trapezium the height is one of the sides (the side at 90° to both parallel sides). If the number of bags is not a whole number, always round **up**: you cannot buy part of a bag, and rounding down would leave some of the field uncovered.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Using the sloping side instead of the perpendicular height.
For a trapezium: forgetting to halve, or multiplying the two parallel sides together instead of adding them.
Using two sides that are not parallel as a and b.
Giving the area in cm instead of cm² (area always has square units).
Mixing units, for example a base in m and a height in cm. Change to one unit first.
In reverse questions, dividing by the height but forgetting to double the trapezium area (or the other way round).

blocks.title: How Checkpoint asks this
items: "Calculate the area of the trapezium/parallelogram." The diagram is often marked NOT TO SCALE and gives extra lengths (sloping sides) you should not use.
Reverse questions: "The area is 60 cm². Work out the height." Write the formula with the numbers in, then solve.
"Show that…" questions: show every step and finish with the exact number given, e.g. '= 40 cm² as required'.
Compound shapes made of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms and trapezia: split, find each area, then add (or subtract).
Shapes on a square grid: count squares for the base and the perpendicular height.
Explain or derive: "Explain why the area of a parallelogram is base × height." Describe cutting and moving the triangle to make a rectangle.
Paper 1 has no calculator: halve the even number first to make the calculation easy.

blocks.title: Area of parallelograms and trapezia — practice
blocks.intro: 14 questions, from easy to Checkpoint-hard. Try them without a calculator first. Give areas in square units.

questions.q: A parallelogram has base 12 cm and perpendicular height 7 cm. Work out its area.
A trapezium has parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm. The perpendicular height is 6 cm. Work out its area.
a and b are the parallel sides of a trapezium and h is its perpendicular height. Which formula gives its area?
questions.e: Two identical trapezia make a parallelogram with base (a + b) and height h, area (a + b)h. One trapezium is half of this: ½(a + b)h.

questions.q: A parallelogram has area 72 cm² and perpendicular height 8 cm. Work out the length of its base.
A trapezium has area 84 cm². Its parallel sides are 9 cm and 15 cm. Work out its perpendicular height.
A trapezium has area 50 cm² and perpendicular height 5 cm. One parallel side is 8 cm. How long is the other parallel side?
questions.e: 50 = ½ × (8 + b) × 5. Double both sides: 100 = (8 + b) × 5. Divide by 5: 8 + b = 20, so b = 12 cm. Check: ½ × 20 × 5 = 50 ✓.

questions.q: Work out the area of PQRS.
questions.e: Base PQ goes from x = 1 to x = 7: 6 cm. Perpendicular height from y = 1 to y = 5: 4 cm. A = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². (Do not count along the sloping side PS.)

questions.p: The shape is made from a rectangle and a trapezium (NOT TO SCALE).

questions.q: Work out the total area of the shape.
questions.e: Rectangle: 10 × 4 = 40 cm². Trapezium: parallel sides 10 cm and 6 cm, height 3 cm: ½ × (10 + 6) × 3 = 8 × 3 = 24 cm². Total = 40 + 24 = 64 cm².

questions.q: Which trapezium has an area of exactly 30 cm²? (a and b are the parallel sides, h is the height.)
c: a = 4 cm, b = 6 cm, h = 3 cm
a = 5 cm, b = 7 cm, h = 4 cm
a = 2 cm, b = 8 cm, h = 6 cm
a = 3 cm, b = 9 cm, h = 6 cm

questions.q: A parallelogram and a rectangle have the same base and the same perpendicular height. Which statement is true?
c: The parallelogram has the bigger area.
The rectangle has the bigger area.
It depends on how long the sloping side is.
questions.e: Both areas are base × perpendicular height, so they are equal. The parallelogram can be cut and rearranged into exactly that rectangle.

questions.q: A garden is a trapezium with parallel sides 12 m and 18 m. The distance between the parallel sides is 9 m. One box of fertiliser covers 20 m². How many boxes are needed to cover the whole garden?
questions.e: Area = ½ × (12 + 18) × 9 = 15 × 9 = 135 m². Boxes: 135 ÷ 20 = 6.75, so 7 boxes are needed (6 boxes cover only 120 m²; round up).

questions.q: Explain how you can use a rectangle to show that the area of a parallelogram is base × perpendicular height. You may draw a diagram.
questions.ms: 1 mark: cut a (right-angled) triangle off one end of the parallelogram along the perpendicular height and move it to the other end, making a rectangle (a clear diagram is acceptable). 1 mark: the rectangle has the same area, with length = base and width = perpendicular height, so area = b × h.
questions.e: Draw the perpendicular height from one top corner down to the base. Cut off the right-angled triangle this makes and slide it to the other end. The two pieces fit together into a rectangle. The rectangle's length is the base b and its width is the perpendicular height h, and no area was lost or added, so area of parallelogram = b × h.

questions.p: Shape A is a trapezium with parallel sides 10 cm and 6 cm and height 5 cm. Shape B is a parallelogram with base 8 cm and height 5 cm.

questions.q: Show that shapes A and B have the same area.
questions.ms: 1 mark: trapezium ½ × (10 + 6) × 5 = 40 (cm²). 1 mark: parallelogram 8 × 5 = 40 (cm²) and a conclusion that they are equal. Both calculations must be shown.
questions.e: A: ½ × (10 + 6) × 5 = ½ × 16 × 5 = 8 × 5 = 40 cm². B: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². Both are 40 cm², so the areas are the same. (Notice: the mean of the parallel sides, (10 + 6) ÷ 2 = 8, equals the base of B.)

blocks.title: Remember
items: Parallelogram: A = base × perpendicular height (it rearranges into a rectangle).
Trapezium: A = ½(a + b)h, where a and b are the parallel sides (two copies make a parallelogram; or split into two triangles).
Always use the perpendicular height, never the sloping side.
Reverse questions: put the numbers into the formula, then use inverse operations.
Areas are in square units: cm², m², mm².
